title: Fighters Destiny
subtitle: Genki / Opus / Anchor · Nintendo 64

body: Fighters Destiny is a Nintendo 64 fighting game whose matches award points for different kinds of victory. A ring-out, throw or knockout can each contribute a different amount toward the total needed to win. The system makes the current score part of deciding how to approach an opponent. A modest opportunity may be enough to finish a match, while another situation makes a riskier technique worthwhile. Punches, kicks and movement remain familiar, but the value of their result changes with the way the exchange ends.

Reducing an opponent's health can leave them briefly dizzy, creating a chance to deliver a finishing move. Surviving that condition allows the fighter to recover, so an advantage has to be converted into a useful result. The arena boundary provides another possible route to points, making position important alongside the current health. The player has to recognise whether to pursue damage, a throw or a push toward the edge. The next successful action matters because of what it completes, not simply how much of the gauge it removes.

Additional modes provide challenges and ways to acquire moves, with a Controller Pak able to preserve an expanded command list. Training against a robot gives space to learn the next technique before using it against another person. Released in 1998, the game was known in Japan as Fighting Cup and later received a sequel. Its strongest idea is the scoring structure: several kinds of successful exchange remain useful, giving two familiar-looking fighters more than one practical reason to change their approach during a match.
